analysis:
Examined the `--disk` work-disk support in SandboxSetupCommand.swift (head 42-46, 67-75, 107-131, 156-189, 289-367, 419-448, 480-491) and the plan/disk parsing plus `SandboxTerminal.choose` in SandboxSetupProgress.swift (head 162-175, 195-204, 486-499).

New behavior:
- The CLI passes `--disk` paths to the installer after `SandboxWorkDisk.absolutePath`. Plan and install runs still use the same downloaded and staged script, so the TB-013/T-061 trust posture is unchanged.
- The CLI checks each work disk's APFS format and ownership before installing.
- At an interactive prompt only (`!confirmed` and `interactiveInput`, line 321), it can run `sudo diskutil enableOwnership` on the volume's mount point after an explicit confirm (lines 327-334). sudo asks the owner for a password. This is an owner-consented privileged action. It is never taken automatically under `--yes` or without a terminal.
- `withInstaller` (482-487) refuses `--disk` when the downloaded script lacks disk support.
- The plan's failure path (435-446) is fail-closed when work disks are given.
- `choose` (486-499) returns 1 (internal disk) on an empty answer or EOF. Its loop ends at EOF, so there is no hang.
- Plan `disks` parsing is display-only; malformed entries are dropped.

Assessment:
- I found no provider inference, attestation, key, or coordinator surface touched. A-001 through A-018 are unaffected.
- The sandbox geteuid != 0 check is retained (line 84).

Items for integration and threat-model maintenance:
- The `SandboxWorkDisk.enableOwnership` implementation is not supplied. It should invoke diskutil with argv (not a shell string) and a fixed `/usr/bin/sudo` path. The mount point comes from `SandboxWorkDisk.volume` or `candidates()`.
- `SandboxInstaller.arguments`/`planArguments` are not supplied. They should pass disk paths as separate argv elements so a path cannot inject installer flags.
- TB-013/A-019 could note that VM images and jobs may now live on operator-selected external APFS volumes. Those controllers sit outside any integrity boundary, similar to T-041's cache-volume caveats. This is a sandbox add-on concern, not provider confidentiality.

I identified no concrete regression.
